title: CompTIA Security+ (SY0-701)
description: Prepares for CompTIA's Security+ exam SY0-701: security controls and cryptography, threats, vulnerabilities and attacks, security architecture and data protection, security operations (hardening, vulnerability management, monitoring, identity and access, incident response) and security program management (governance, risk, third parties, compliance, audits and awareness). Practised with performance-based questions (firewall rules, log analysis, matching, placing devices on a network, certificates, risk calculations) and hands-on labs on two simulated Linux servers.
disclaimer: Cert Lab is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by CompTIA. CompTIA and Security+ are trademarks of CompTIA, Inc. This course follows the topics of CompTIA's public exam objectives for Security+ SY0-701 as Cert Lab understood them in 2026 (five domains: General security concepts, about 12%; Threats, vulnerabilities and mitigations, about 22%; Security architecture, about 18%; Security operations, about 28%; Security program management and oversight, about 20%). The weights are approximate to the published outline, and CompTIA updates its exams: check the current objectives on comptia.org before you book. Every lesson, card, question, performance-based question and lab was written for Cert Lab in its own words; none comes from CompTIA's exams, objectives text or any study guide. The practice servers are a simulation written by Cert Lab.
examNote: A Cert Lab practice exam in the style of CompTIA's Security+: up to 90 items in 90 minutes, mostly single and multiple answer questions with short scenarios, plus a few performance-based questions (PBQs: firewall rules, log analysis, drag-and-drop matching, placing devices on a network, certificates, risk calculations) that give partial credit. You can flag items for review and see a review screen before you submit. Scores are shown from 100 to 900 with 750 to pass, like CompTIA's score reports; CompTIA doesn't publish how it scales scores, so Cert Lab's score is only an approximation (100 plus your share of the points times 800). Results are shown per domain, and the review explains every answer.
examHint: One item at a time: Next and Previous move between items, Flag for review marks one to come back to, and Review shows every item before you submit. Performance-based questions give partial credit, so answer every part you can.
aboutMachines: The practice servers are the RHCSA course's two simulated RHEL 9 machines, server1 (192.168.50.11) and server2 (192.168.50.12), root password redhat. The Security+ labs use them for hands-on security work: file hashes and integrity checks, permissions and least privilege, SSH hardening, firewall rules, reading logs, password policy and certificates (an openssl-like tool written for Cert Lab). The companies, people, addresses and logs in the questions are made up.
